One thing worth checking before this merges. AWS's own Python sample for this endpoint ([aws-samples/amazon-transcribe-streaming-python-websockets](https://github.com/aws-samples/amazon-transcribe-streaming-python-websockets/blob/main/example.py)) leaves `ping_interval` at the default but sets `ping_timeout=None`:

```python
async with websockets.connect(request_url,
                              extra_headers=extra_headers,
                              ping_timeout=None,
                              ) as websocket:
```

So pings are clearly accepted: the sample sends one every 20s, and `_verify_connection` in `websocket_service.py` already pings this endpoint on every reconnect. But AWS turned off the part that waits for the pong.

If the endpoint doesn't answer pings reliably, restoring the default `ping_timeout` would close healthy connections about 40s in, which is worse than the half-open case this fixes. I can't run it without AWS credentials. Could someone who has them stream a minute or two through this branch and confirm the connection survives past 40s?
